tests.mutation: Yielding.WellClear cited collision-hazard-proximity's `§ 107.37(b)` (`MapEntries.CollisionHazardProximity.Locator` for `MapEntries.WellClear.Locator`), so the decline named the other constituent of § 107.37; this test went red. It went red too with the reason wrong (`UnresolvedReason.UnsupportedRule` for `UnresolvedReason.RequiresInterpretation`). Citing right-of-way's locator (`MapEntries.RightOfWay.Locator`) did NOT turn it red: both entries cite `§ 107.37(a)`, so the locator cannot tell them apart and only Attempted names well-clear.

Yielding.WellClear declined with the correspondence row's bare wording, naming no reason (`$"resolve the map entry '{MapEntries.WellClear.Id}'"` for the message naming "well clear" as undefined, the exception to the prohibition on passing over, under or ahead, and that § 107.37(a) states no measure for it), so the decline cited where without saying why; this test went red. It went red too with Handlers.WellClear answering the open question instead of delegating to the rule (`Resolution<object>.FromValue(true)` for `Yielding.WellClear(Demand(...))`), which broke the assertion that the entry point's resolution is exactly `Yielding.WellClear(NoWaiver)` — that mutation turned all six of these tests red.

Handlers.WellClear took the caller's word for the entry, as though it were `kind: assertion` (`request.Assertions == RuleRequest.Empty ? Yielding.WellClear(Demand(...)) : Resolution<object>.FromValue(request.Assertions.Asserted(request.EntryId))` for `Yielding.WellClear(Demand(...))`), so a caller who asserted well-clear true resolved to true instead of the decline; this test went red, and only this one.

Yielding.WellClear handed the gate a statement that no waiver is in force (`waiver with { InForce = false }` for `waiver`), so a stated waiver was not honoured and the entry declined RequiresInterpretation citing § 107.37(a) instead of OutsideCurrentScope citing § 107.205; this test went red. It went red too with Yielding.WellClear naming right-of-way as the suspended entry (`MapEntries.RightOfWay` for `MapEntries.WellClear` in the call to Waivers.Suspension), so Attempted named right-of-way rather than well-clear — the two entries share the locator `§ 107.37(a)`, so what was attempted is the only thing that tells them apart.
Handlers.WellClear defaulted a missing statement to none held (`request.Waiver ?? WaiverStatement.NoneHeld(Yielding.Regulation, "the engine")` for `Demand(request.Waiver, ...)`); this test went red.

Yielding.WellClear compared the statement's regulation with itself (`waiver.Regulation` for `Regulation` in the call to Waivers.Suspension), so a waiver of § 107.51 suspended § 107.37(a); this test went red.
